extracted.intended_audience: IP statisticians, patent office staff, policymakers, researchers and analysts using WIPO patent statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Methodology and definitional guidance for compiling, interpreting and presenting WIPO patent statistics (applications, grants, patent families, origins, resident/non-resident breakdowns, and technology-field mappings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent family definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent family is defined as patent applications interlinked by one or more of the following: priority claim, Patent Cooperation Treaty national phase entry, continuation, continuation-in-part, internal priority, and addition or division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent families here include only those families associated with patent applications for inventions and exclude those associated with utility model applications. Used to compile family-count indicators (A23, A24, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign-oriented patent family definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A special subset of patent families comprises foreign-oriented patent families. This includes only those patent families that have at least one filing office different from the office of the applicant’s country of origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some foreign-oriented patent families include only one filing office, because applicants may choose to file directly with a foreign office (example: a Canadian applicant filing directly with the USPTO). Used to construct 'foreign-oriented' family indicators (A25–A26).

rubrics_metrics.name: Origin of an application/grant (how origin is determined)
rubrics_metrics.description: The origin of a patent application is determined by the residence of the first named applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Origin data are based on absolute counts (see below). Origin-based indicators include resident applications and applications filed abroad (A17 and related tables).

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute count rule for regional offices
rubrics_metrics.description: For an absolute count, applications (and grants) filed at regional offices are counted once, rather than being considered equivalent to multiple applications (or grants) in the respective member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This counting rule is applied for origin data and grant counts so that filings at regional offices (e.g., EPO) are not multiplied across member states when producing origin/office totals. Mentioned repeatedly (A17, A19, A21 notes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident vs non-resident classification and contribution breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Data and charts break total growth (applications or grants) at each office into contributions from resident applications/grants and non-resident applications/grants (resident share (%) and non-resident share (%)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charts show how overall growth or decline is decomposed into resident and non-resident contributions; examples explain percentage-point contributions (e.g., Thailand example, EPO example). Use resident/non-resident splits to interpret office-level changes (A8, A10, A14, A16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution on comparing applications and grants in the same year
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination process can take a long time therefore there is invariably a time lag between application and grant dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For this reason, data on applications for a given year should not be compared with data on grants for that same year. Differences across offices in grants depend on examination capacity and procedural delays (A13 note).

rubrics_metrics.name: Published application timing (publication lag)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data refer to published patent applications. There is a minimum 18-month delay between application date and publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published-application series therefore reflect filing activity with at least an 18-month lag; users should account for this when interpreting trends (A29 note).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of utility model applications from family indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent families here include only those families associated with patent applications for inventions and exclude those associated with utility model applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Family-based indicators and technology-field distributions are limited to invention patent applications (A23/A24 notes).

rubrics_metrics.name: IPC-to-technology-field mapping method
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO’s International Patent Classification (IPC) technology concordance table was used to convert IPC symbols into 35 corresponding fields of technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An electronic version of the IPC technology concordance table is available at WIPO; this mapping underlies all technology-field breakdowns (A27–A30 notes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for 'top' offices/origins
rubrics_metrics.description: Top-five, top-20 (or top-15) offices and origins were selected based on available totals for the reference year(s) (for example, the top five offices were selected based on the 2024 totals; the top 15 origins based on 2021–2023 totals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should note that 'top' selections are sample-based and reflect data availability and the chosen reference period (various chart notes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of relative specialization index
rubrics_metrics.description: A positive relative specialization index value for a technology indicates that a country has a relatively high share of patent filings related to that technology field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The index is computed for selected technology fields and origins (A30); users should interpret positive/negative values as relative specialization or underrepresentation respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'foreign-oriented' family special case (direct foreign filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some foreign-oriented patent families include only one filing office because applicants may choose to file directly with a foreign office (example: a Canadian applicant files directly with the USPTO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies that a foreign-oriented family does not require multiple filing offices to appear in the stat series — direct foreign filings are included (A25/A26 explanation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sources and integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistics and charts are compiled from the WIPO Statistics Database and the EPO PATSTAT database (dates: September 2025 cited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users referencing or replicating indicators should use the same source combination and note the date of extraction for consistency (appears in multiple figure notes).
